restated: Let f(q,r) be defined by the Brouwer recurrence (MISSION section 2). Write d_n=f(n,n), D_{<n}={d_a : 0<=a<n}, R_n={f(n,b) : 0<=b<n}, delta_n=#{a<n : d_a>d_n}, and c_n=|(R_n \ D_{<n}) cap [1,d_n)|. Then for every n>=1, d_n = n + 1 - delta_n + c_n exactly. This is an exact identity; it claims no bound.
ledger_statement: EXACT MEX-SANDWICH IDENTITY (unconditional; an identity, no bound claimed). With d_n=f(n,n), D_{<n}={d_a:a<n}, R_n={f(n,b):b<n}, delta_n=#{a<n: d_a>d_n}, c_n=|(R_n \ D_{<n}) cap [1,d_n)|: for every n>=1, d_n = n+1-delta_n+c_n. Proof: (n,n) is a mex cell because f(n-1,n)=d_{n-1}>n-1 (Sheiner L4.1 = #G07 s8.3), with mex set D_{<n} u R_n; the d_a are distinct since d_n is not in D_{<n}; R_n subset [1,d_n) by Sheiner L4.1 + L2.3(a); counting [1,d_n) gives d_n-1 = (n-delta_n)+c_n. Premise (P) of the earlier version is now proved, not assumed.

verdicts.gap_description: No gap found. Each step follows from the recurrence plus the two explicitly stated inputs (S4.1, S2.3a); the load-bearing branch analysis (d_{n-1} >= n kills branch 2 at (n,n)) is correct even at n = 1, and the counting step in Step 3 is a disjoint split of [1, d_n) justified exactly by Step 1(2) and Step 2 distinctness. Minor bookkeeping: the metadata says '(none cited)' while the proof prints two Sheiner lemmas as inputs; their statements are given and were verified computationally, so this is not a mathematical gap.

All quantities (delta_n, c_n) are computable from the recurrence, so the identity is effective as a computable rewriting of d_n, but the proof yields no computable bound on N(r) — by its own statement it is not an attempt at the effectivity target, so the effectivity trap does not apply (no existence-only constant is passed off as a bound).

verdicts.gap_description: No non-following step found. Step 1's branch check is valid (f(n-1,n)=f(n-1,n-1)=d_{n-1}>=n since d_{n-1}>n-1 is an integer, so branch 2 does not fire at (n,n)); the mex set is exactly D_{<n} u R_n; Step 2 correctly combines (S2.3a) distinctness with (S4.1) maximality to get R_n subset [1,d_n) and pairwise distinct d_a; Step 3's count of [1,d_n) is exact and disjoint, giving d_n = n+1-delta_n+c_n. The only external inputs are the two precisely stated Sheiner lemmas (S4.1, S2.3a), which I verified numerically at every n<=10000; minor caveats: the submission's 'Results cited as already established: (none cited)' header conflicts with its declared Inputs (S4.1, S2.3a), and I could not bibliographically verify the arXiv citations (sandbox network refused) — a formatting gap, not a logical one.

verdicts.effectivity_check: No computable bound is produced — and none is claimed: the submission states verbatim 'This is an exact identity. It asserts no bound and makes no effectivity claim.' There is no effectivity trap here: every term (d_n, delta_n, c_n) is computable from the recurrence in finite time, so the identity is a genuine exact rewriting, but it yields no bound whatsoever on N(r) or on the period; it only reframes d_n - n = 1 + c_n - delta_n. For the project's stated target (an explicit computable bound on N(r)) this submission is a restatement, not a step with an effective conclusion.
